title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Anchoring a bio-inspired LnCo3 oxygen-evolution cluster to P-doped g-C3N4 through a Co–P linkage lets the cluster accept photogenerated holes, while Ln3+ stabilizes anionic intermediates and the cobalt centers share the oxidative load.
explanation: Mixed-valence LnCoIICoIII2 resembles {CaMn4O5} except for a missing cubane vertex and an extra Nd–O–Co bridge. A 1.05 wt% NdCo3/PCN loading gave 297.7 and 148.9 μmol h−1 g−1 H2 and O2, 7.2 times pure PCN. fs-TA, XPS, and DFT indicate hole transfer to the cluster, stabilization of negative intermediates by Ln3+, and use of non-aqua cobalt ions as hole reservoirs.
scope: LnCo3 clusters covalently supported on phospho-doped graphitic carbon nitride for overall water splitting.
conditions: UV–vis irradiation, λ > 300 nm, pure water; stoichiometric H2:O2 near 2:1.
caveats: Activity is loading-dependent; 1.05 wt% NdCo3/PCN is the reported optimum, not every loading.
